title: Export formats, documented schema and self-service export
status_rationale: UNB-TEN-016 requires an exportable, evidence-complete logical dataset and portability protocol per partner; UNB-KNOW-038 requires versioned schema exports; UNB-PLAT-003 requires Folio for human-readable artifacts. Nothing is built.
target_answer: Customers can, without Echelon involvement, export their complete tenant dataset as versioned, documented open formats: JSON Lines or Parquet for records and events with a published JSON Schema per record type, CSV views for common tables, original-format documents with a manifest, and PDF/A renderings of statements and letters. The export schema is versioned with change notes and backward-compatibility rules, and the same schema is published to prospects before contract.
intended_practice: Specify the logical export schema alongside the domain model; build self-service export early, since it also serves backup verification and migration.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify a complete, exportable logical dataset per partner with versioned schemas. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Can Folio produce PDF/A or another archival format? Folio archival capability is unverified (UNB-PLAT-003).

title: Export completeness: full history, audit trail, decisions and vendor-generated records
status_rationale: UNB-TEN-016 requires an evidence-complete dataset; UNB-TEN-012 and UNB-TEN-013 require verifiable equivalence on migration. Public DAF administrator MSAs reviewed in daf-landscape return only customer-provided materials, not vendor-generated records.
target_answer: The export contains everything the sponsor needs to continue operating and defend past decisions: the full append-only event history including corrections and reversals, current and historical balances and unit values, all grants with approvals, reviewer rationale, eligibility and sanctions screening snapshots, policy versions in force, overrides with authority, payment instructions and confirmations, communications, documents, consents and preferences, AI agent recommendations and the human decisions on them, and audit logs. Each export carries a manifest with record counts, control totals and hashes so the customer can verify completeness and reconcile balances independently. Exports are strictly tenant-scoped.
intended_practice: Define completeness as the full event stream plus documents; contractually commit that vendor-generated records are customer data for export purposes.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify an evidence-complete exportable dataset per partner, preserving provenance, corrections and audit chain. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Which third-party licensed data (for example charity intelligence sources) cannot be included in exports under source licenses (SOC2-028, UNB-KNOW-038)?

history.change: BL-021: set institutional_acceptance to unknown (prior 'likely' was unsourced agent judgment, kept in supporting_arguments) and added an unvalidated-acceptance note to opposing_arguments (OBJ-VRM-019, OBJ-SKEPTIC-014).

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants to be able to leave without losing the history needed to operate and defend past decisions.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Sponsor exits with balances but without approvals, rationale or audit trail, and cannot answer an IRS or donor inquiry about a past grant.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional 'return of customer data' clauses often cover only customer-provided materials and are verified only at exit, too late.
challenge.legally_required: Not generally legally required; sponsors' own recordkeeping obligations make it practically necessary.
challenge.contractually_required: Increasingly negotiated by institutional customers; public DAF administrator templates reviewed do not provide it.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendors have treated generated records and audit logs as vendor property.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Because the authoritative store is an append-only event log, a complete export is the event stream itself; nothing must be reconstructed.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Scheduled full exports to customer-controlled storage during the contract make exit a non-event.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Periodic export manifests with control totals give continuous evidence of portability.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Continuous scheduled export to customer-owned storage with reconcilable manifests.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes: customers can load and reconcile exports themselves.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Licensed third-party content and other tenants' shared facts cannot be included; the export is complete only for sponsor-owned data.
challenge.conventional_cost: Low to promise, high to deliver at exit under pressure.
challenge.alternative_risks: Exports to customer storage expand the attack surface and require customer-side security.
supporting_arguments: Turns exit readiness into something tested continuously.
Directly addresses a documented market gap.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; it exceeds conventional terms.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Exported audit logs may reveal Echelon internal operational details.
Customers may not maintain or test their export copies.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: APIs and bulk programmatic access for data retrieval
status_rationale: UNB-API-STD-001 defines API standards; UNB-XIN-SAS-004 defines thin event subscriptions; UNB-XIN-SAS-007 terminates partner API clients at partner exit. No bulk export API exists.
target_answer: Customers have documented APIs to retrieve all data incrementally (by event sequence) and in bulk, with rate limits that permit a full extraction within a defined window, and no extraction fees. API access for export continues through the termination assistance period even after other access ends.
intended_practice: Design an incremental event-feed API from the start; set extraction-grade rate limits for export endpoints.

title: Migration assistance into and out of the platform
status_rationale: CNV-EXP-002 requires importing each donor's full fund history from a predecessor platform with a reconciliation report; UNB-TEN-011..013 specify governed, verifiable migration with a single authoritative writer; UNB-CUST-023 preserves history in custodian migrations; UNB-XIN-SAS-007 governs partner exits.
target_answer: Echelon runs migrations in both directions with the same method: a governed plan, a consistent cutover point, verifiable source and destination equivalence, independent ledger reconciliation, mapping tables for fund, grant and party identifiers, and a reconciliation report signed off by the sponsor. Parallel run is supported for a defined period without two authoritative writers. Outbound migration assistance is priced in advance in the contract.
current_practice: Not established. No migration has been performed.
intended_practice: Build the inbound importer first (it is required to win customers) and reuse it as the specification for outbound assistance.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify full-history inbound migration with reconciliation and governed, verifiable tenant migration. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.

title: Interoperability with other DAF platforms, grant networks and donor-level portability
status_rationale: No industry-standard DAF data schema was identified in the reviewed research. UNB-KNOW-038 calls for versioned schema exports; CNV-EXP-002 contemplates networked grant-payment partners; UNB-SUCC-014 warns cross-sponsor portability is not automatic.
target_answer: Echelon publishes its export and interchange schemas openly under a license that lets customers and competing platforms implement them, supports exchange with networked grant-payment partners in their published formats, and gives donors a portable statement of their fund history when a fund transfers to another sponsor. Contracts do not restrict customers from sharing schemas or exports with competing vendors.
current_practice: Unknown; no interoperability work or standard identified.
intended_practice: Survey whether any DAF data interchange standard exists; publish the Unbound export schema.
customer_statement: Echelon is not aware of an industry data standard for DAF administration and has not yet published its own interchange schema.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Does any DAF or charitable giving data interchange standard exist (for example among grant-payment networks), and would adopting it help or constrain Unbound?
